summary: D. S. Subbaramaiya worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.

D. Srinivasachar was an Indology scholar who succeeded Rudrapatna Shamasastry. Attested from 1931 to 1933, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore.

Dagfinn Føllesdal (1932–2026) was a philosopher and linguist. He earned degrees at the University of Oslo and Harvard, where he completed his Ph.D. under Willard Van Orman Quine. He taught at Harvard, Stanford, and the University of Oslo.

Dagmar Schwerk specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg from 2007 to 2017, completing her doctorate under Dorji Wangchuk, and became a professor at the University of Leipzig around 2022.

Born in 1932, Dagpo Rinpoche works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche, and later taught scholars including David Seyfort Ruegg and Anne-Marie Blondeau.

Taichi Tado specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held teaching posts at Waseda University (attested 2020), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020–2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Daiei Kaneko (1881–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa, later holding posts at Toyo University and Otani University (~1916–1951), as well as founding Koho Gakuen.
Daigo Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied and served as a research student (研究生) at Ryukoku University (attested 2006).

Daijaku Judith Kinst specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She held a faculty post at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and is attested as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 2026.

Daiju Sasaki (born 1977) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from 1996 to 2006. He held teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2015 and ~2018) and at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

Daijō Tokiwa (1870–1945) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, later holding professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, among other institutional roles.

Dainin Katagiri (1928–1990) was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar. He studied at Eihei-ji and Komazawa University, served as priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission, became interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (1870–1966) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Waseda and the University of Tokyo, he held professorships at Otani University and Columbia University, and founded the Eastern Buddhist Society and Matsugaoka Bunko.

Daishun Ueyama (1934–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his academic career at Ryukoku University as an associate professor, professor, and university president.

Daito Shimaji (1875–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku and Otani universities, he taught at Komazawa, Rissho, and Toyo universities, as well as Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1923.

Dale S. Wright (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann, and served as a professor at Occidental College from around 1980 to 2017.

Dalsukh Malvania (1910–2000) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, the University of Toronto, and MS University of Baroda, and served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology.
Damchö Gyatso studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev specialized in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his degrees from Lancaster and Oxford, served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, and co-founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics.
